paragraphs: A Bag for Every Child, posted by Mia. On Thursday, Teacher Kim gave the Explorers a talk about jobs. She told us a story about a woman from our town. Her name was Rose Hartley, and she lived many years ago. The Explorers sat quietly, and Teacher Kim spoke slowly. She had many occupations, and each one taught her something new. I took notes, and Lily drew a picture of a bag.

Rose was born in a small house next to the market. At the age of sixteen, she found a job in a small bag company. The workroom was big, and many machines made a loud noise. She was a cleaner, and she came to work before the sun came up. She cleaned the floor, the windows, and the long tables. Every worker said hello to her, and she learned all the names.

After two years, the boss gave her a new job at the front desk. She became the receptionist of the company. She was kind to everybody, and the visitors liked her. A receptionist smiles at visitors and answers the telephone. She learned who bought the bags and what they wanted. She wrote their words in a small book.

At the age of thirty, she had an idea. Many children in the town carried their books in old paper bags, and the bags broke in the rain. She wanted a strong bag with good straps for every pupil. She asked the boss to make it, but he said, "No, it costs too much." So she left the company, and she started her own.

Her company began with one machine and three staff. The staff made twenty bags a day. The first bag was blue, and it kept the books dry. She chose blue because it was her favorite color. In ten years, the company had fifty staff. Every school in the town bought her bags. The woman was now a businesswoman, and her work was a great success. She paid her staff well, and she never forgot her first job.

Teacher Kim showed us an old bag from that company. It was blue and strong, and it still looked good. "Look at the straps," said Teacher Kim. "Every child can carry it with a school uniform." The company is still in the old market today. Which occupation do you want for your career?
